 $ cd
 /Users/USER/Documents/projects/fleetmux-wt-acceptance42
 && git add README.md scripts/install_release.sh
 tests/test_install_release.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
 fix(scripts): keep the install log, own only the created
 release dir, print the release start command (M60)

 Installer review r1 (reviewer-1/linux-delivery-review.json)
 found three P1s in the 9c20a32f installer:

 - P1-01: `--test` wrote $REL/release-tests.log and
 cleanup() rm -rf'd $REL, so a red UTM run lost the
   whole log. The complete log now lives at
 $RELEASES/.logs/<sha>-<ts>-<pid>.log (outside the release
   dir) and its path is printed on failure and on success.
 - P1-02: `[ -e "$REL" ]` + `mkdir -p` was not atomic and
 <sha> was unvalidated, so a second install could
   join and then delete the first run's release, and a
 non-hex <sha> sent `rm -rf` outside $RELEASES.
   <sha> must now be 7-40 hex (upper case normalised; older
 short-SHA callers keep working) and the release
   dir is created with a bare `mkdir`; CREATED is only set
 by the run whose mkdir succeeded.
 - P1-03: nothing printed or recorded <release>/bin on PATH,
 so a normal shell ran the stale ~/.local/bin
   build. Success now prints `PATH=<release>/bin:$PATH
 <release>/.venv/bin/fleetmux-py --help` (console
   script first, `python -m fleetmux.fleet` fallback) and
 records it as `start_command`.

 Also the recorded items: manifest.json is parsed with
 json.load instead of a sed regex (a valid
 pretty-printed manifest is accepted, a non-JSON one is
 refused with the parse error), and installed.json
 is written by json.dump and re-parsed before the release is
 declared ready, so a --tool-sha with a quote
 or a path with backslashes stays valid JSON. The
 interpreter is now picked before the binaries are
 verified because it does the parsing.

 README gets the release-install usage (release-local bin/,
 log location, start command, hex <sha>).

 Targeted: tests/test_install_release.py 22 passed (13
 existing + 9 new); against the 9c20a32f installer
 the same file is 8 failed / 14 passed. reviewer-1's
 repro_m52.py re-run from a copy with a stub that
 implements `python - <script>`: R1 LOG KEPT, R2a canary
 survived, R2b release survived, R3-hex refused,
 R4 valid manifest accepted, R5 valid JSON, R6 console
 command printed. The application release stays
 35670632 source + binaries; this commit changes only how it
 is installed.
 EOF

 Commit 1: 0622dba1.

 Now commit 2: setup_fixture.py daemon exec sleep 3600 vs
 "never exits on its own".

 Fix design:
 - Replace the daemon command with a POSIX infinite wait
   that both macOS and Linux support and that is terminable:
   exec /bin/sh -c 'while :; do sleep 3600; done'.
 - Keep the printed synthetic marker line.
 - Update the module docstring line 9.
 - Maybe add a comment explaining the baseline observation
   (fixture-only repair 2026-10-31T15:36, no product code)
   and that sleep infinity is GNU-only.

 Also: "保留可清理进程组及合成fixture标识" — keep cleanable
 process group and synthetic fixture marker. The
 spawn_window runs bash -lc 'cd <cwd> && exec <command>' per
 the docstring. So the pane's process is the exec'd sh loop
 → killing the pane kills it; and the loop's sleep 3600
 child is in the same process group → cleanable. Good;
 document that.

 Should I also add a marker env/print? The current printf
 prints 'fixture daemon — no real task'. I'll extend to
 include a stable synthetic marker token so acceptance can
 grep: e.g. A42_FIXTURE_DAEMON=synthetic. Hmm, "合成fixture
 标识" = synthetic fixture identifier. The existing printed
 line is the marker. I'll keep it and add the token in the
 same line:

 printf 'fixture daemon — synthetic, no real task
 (A42_FIXTURE=synthetic-daemon)\\n'
